signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard records USD as the weekly leader at +1.267% across 9 pairs while SEK lags at −1.074% across 2 pairs, generating an extreme 2.342% bilateral performance spread. The Fed policy rate of 4.0% against the Riksbank at 1.75% provides a substantial 225bp nominal policy advantage alongside an ESI divergence where USD prints +7.2 against SEK at −29.2. USD/SEK spot trades at 9.861, standing well clear of its rising SMA20/50/200 stack at 9.597, 9.596, and 9.353. Macro momentum and wider yield support heavily reinforce the upside, though the BEER valuation model notes spot is stretched at +1.83σ above fair value. Sustained divergence persists while US curve dynamics remain in a bear-flattener regime. Trade bias: Long USD/SEK, policy and data divergence trend continuation. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Spread compresses below 0.80% as US curve steepening unwinds the dollar premium.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning Exhaustion
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7106, hovering just above its daily SMA50 at 0.708 while testing resistance below the SMA20 at 0.717. CFTC data shows leveraged funds holding an extended net long of +48,379 contracts, sitting at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +1.72. The latest reporting week reveals an outflow of −1,871 contracts alongside an Australian unemployment rate surprise of +0.2pp to 4.5% (a +2.50σ shock), signalling labor market softening. Despite a supportive +71bp AONIA over SOFR carry buffer, the options market displays caution via a −0.72 25d risk reversal put skew. The combination of stalled speculative additions and deteriorating domestic employment points to upside trend exhaustion. Trade bias: Short AUD/USD, positioning squeeze risk on stretched speculative longs. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep. Risk: Sustained close above 0.7170 validating trend continuation.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Retail Extreme vs Macro Carry Headwinds
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5725, remaining locked beneath its descending SMA20 at 0.5878 and SMA50 at 0.5858. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows an extreme 89% long reading, diverging sharply from institutional positioning where leveraged funds hold −18,092 net short contracts at the 8th percentile of their 52-week range. The Fed-RBNZ OIS differential reflects a +125bp carry advantage favoring the dollar, reinforced by restrictive US real policy rates of +1.59% against New Zealand's +0.41%. Despite Q2 GDP printing slightly above consensus at 0.2% quarter-on-quarter, domestic activity shows underlying household strain. Retail traders attempting to catch the bottom run heavy liquidation risk against prevailing institutional flow and adverse carry. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, contrarian alignment against retail extreme positioning. Catalyst: New Zealand Trade Balance at 22:45 UTC. Risk: RBNZ delivers an unexpected hawkish repricing at its next meeting, triggering a short-covering rally.
